record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Suppose Ω ⊂ C satisfies the arclength null-quadrature identity ∫_{∂Ω} g(z) ds(z) = 0 for every g in E^1(Ω). Does this condition force the unit tangent vector on ∂Ω to admit an analytic continuation throughout Ω?

evidence.quote: before trying to answer the Question above, one may first approach a simpler question: Does the vanishing of integrals stated in (3.1) for all g ∈ E^1(Ω) guarantee the analytic continuation of the tangent vector to all of Ω?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a domain with rectifiable boundary $\partial\Omega$, and let $ds$ denote arclength measure on $\partial\Omega$. Recall that the Smirnov class $E^1(\Omega)$ consists of those holomorphic functions $g$ on $\Omega$ for which there exists a sequence of rectifiable Jordan curves $\{\Gamma_n\}$ exhausting $\Omega$ such that $\sup_n \int_{\Gamma_n} |g(z)|\, |dz| < \infty$; equivalently, $g$ has nontangential boundary values in $L^1(\partial\Omega, ds)$ and is recovered by the Cauchy integral of these boundary values.

Call $\Omega$ an arclength null-quadrature domain (ALNQD) if
$$\int_{\partial\Omega} g(z)\, ds(z) = 0 \quad \text{for every } g \in E^1(\Omega).$$

Let $T(z)$ denote the unit tangent vector to $\partial\Omega$ (defined a.e. on the rectifiable boundary), viewed as a complex-valued function on $\partial\Omega$.

Question: Does the ALNQD condition above force $T$ to extend from $\partial\Omega$ to an analytic function on all of $\Omega$? That is, does there exist a function $h$ holomorphic in $\Omega$ whose nontangential boundary values agree a.e. on $\partial\Omega$ with the unit tangent vector $T$?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2020 preprint (published 2022 in the Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society) by Khavinson and Lundberg establishes the analytic continuation of the unit tangent vector to all of Ω for arclength null-quadrature domains having finitely many smooth boundary components, thereby proving the existence of a "roof function" in this setting. The general case (without restriction on the number/regularity of boundary components) does not appear to be fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: A note on arclength null quadrature domains
status_evidence.snippet: We prove the existence of a roof function for arclength null quadrature domains having finitely many boundary components.
status_evidence.claim: The tangent continuation problem is resolved under the assumption of finitely many boundary components.

status_evidence.title: A note on arclength null quadrature domains - Bull. LMS 2022
status_evidence.snippet: Published version in Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society, 2022, by Khavinson and Lundberg.
status_evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed publication establishing the partial result.
